result.markdown: --- title: "Session 2 — Kaplan-Meier Curves" subtitle: "Estimating survival · medians and landmarks · confidence bands · groups and risk tables · Lab 2" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 1: censoring, the Surv object, rates - Today: **estimate and draw the survival curve** without assuming a constant rate - By the end you can: - fit and read a **Kaplan-Meier** curve - report **survival at a time point** and the **median** (or "not reached") - draw curves by group with a **number-at-risk table** ::: # Topic 1 — How the estimate is built {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## A step function At each **event time**, survival drops by the fraction who die among those **still at risk**; **censored** patients leave the risk set without causing a drop. ::: {.eq} S(t) = Π (1 − d~i~ / n~i~) over event times ≤ t ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} toy <- tibble(time = c(2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 8), status = c(1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1)) summary(survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, toy)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: survfit(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = toy) time n.risk n.event survival std.err lower 95% CI upper 95% CI 2 6 1 0.833 0.152 0.583 1 3 5 1 0.667 0.192 0.379 1 5 3 1 0.444 0.222 0.167 1 8 1 1 0.000 NaN NA NA ``` ::: ::: ## Reading the toy example ::: {.incremental} - At time 2: 6 at risk, 1 dies: 1 × 5/6 = 0.83 - At time 3: 5 at risk, 1 dies and 1 is censored: 0.83 × 4/5 = 0.67 - The censored patient **counts in the denominator until censored**, then leaves ::: ## The overall curve ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} km <- survfit(Surv(time_months, status) ~ 1, data = tb) km ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: survfit(formula = Surv(time_months, status) ~ 1, data = tb) n events median 0.95LCL 0.95UCL [1,] 600 113 NA NA NA ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggsurvfit(km) + add_confidence_interval() + labs(x = "Months since starting treatment", y = "Survival probability") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s2_kaplan_meier_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: # Topic 2 — Reading the curve {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Survival at a time ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(km, times = c(6, 12, 18)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: survfit(formula = Surv(time_months, status) ~ 1, data = tb) time n.risk n.event survival std.err lower 95% CI upper 95% CI 6 490 76 0.870 0.0140 0.843 0.897 12 439 20 0.833 0.0156 0.803 0.864 18 244 17 0.796 0.0173 0.763 0.831 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} "Survival at 12 months was **83%** (95% CI 80–86%)." Time points beyond the **longest follow-up** (here about 24 months) cannot be estimated. ::: ## The median survival time ::: {.incremental} - The **median** is the time at which the curve **crosses 0.5** - Here fewer than half the patients died, so the curve **never reaches 0.5**: the median is **not reached** (`NA`) - Report **survival at fixed times** (12, 24 months) or the **restricted mean** instead - Never replace "not reached" with the median of the observed times ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(km)$table[c("records", "events", "median")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` records events median 600 113 NA ``` ::: ::: ## Confidence and the tail ::: {.warn} The curve is **least reliable at the right end**, where **few patients remain at risk**: confidence bands widen and a single death moves the curve a lot. Always show the **number at risk** and avoid over-reading the tail. ::: # Topic 3 — Curves by group {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## HIV-positive and negative ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} km_grp <- survfit(Surv(time_months, status) ~ hiv, data = tb) summary(km_grp, times = 12)$surv |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.85 0.72 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggsurvfit(km_grp) + add_confidence_interval() + add_risktable() + scale_ggsurvfit(x_scales = list(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6))) + labs(x = "Months since starting treatment", y = "Survival probability") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s2_kaplan_meier_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Positive patients have **lower survival** throughout - **Overlapping bands** early on; separation grows - The **risk table** shows how many remain: only **63** HIV-positive patients started, so the right end is thin ::: ## Reporting a Kaplan-Meier analysis ::: {.good} - **Number of patients and events** per group - **Median follow-up** (reverse KM) - **Survival at fixed times** with 95% CI, or the median with CI if reached - The **figure** with number at risk, a clear axis and the **log-rank p-value** (Session 3) ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 2 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `survival-workshop/labs/lab2_km.R` - `survfit()` · `summary(times = )` · the median - `ggsurvfit()` with confidence band and risk table - curves by HIV status ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s2q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="eyk5wx.mugnt2" data-show="RmV3ZXIgdGhhbiBoYWxmIG9mIHRoZSBwYXRpZW50cyBoYWQgZGllZCBieSB0aGUgZW5kIG9m IGZvbGxvdy11cA==" data-explain="VGhlIG1lZGlhbiBpcyB3aGVyZSB0aGUgY3VydmUgY3Jvc3NlcyAwLjUuIElmIHN1cnZpdmFs IHN0YXlzIGFib3ZlIDAuNSB0byB0aGUgZW5kIG9mIGZvbGxvdy11cCwgdGhlIG1lZGlhbiBp cyBub3QgcmVhY2hlZDsgcmVwb3J0IHN1cnZpdmFsIGF0IGZpeGVkIHRpbWVzIGluc3RlYWQu "} In a Kaplan-Meier analysis the median survival time is reported as 'not reached'. What does this mean? - The patients were followed for too short a time to be analysed - The median could not be calculated because of missing data in the file - Fewer than half of the patients had died by the end of follow-up - More than half of the patients in the whole cohort were censored ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s2q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="eykj5l.muh2ae" data-show="VGhleSBzdGF5IGF0IHJpc2sgdW50aWwgY2Vuc29yZWQsIHRoZW4gbGVhdmUgd2l0aCBubyBk cm9w" data-explain="Q2Vuc29yZWQgcGF0aWVudHMgY291bnQgYW1vbmcgdGhvc2UgYXQgcmlzayB1cCB0byB0aGVp ciBjZW5zb3JpbmcgdGltZSwgdGhlbiBsZWF2ZS4gVGhleSBuZXZlciBjYXVzZSBhIHN0ZXAg ZG93biwgYnV0IHRoZXkgc2hyaW5rIHRoZSBkZW5vbWluYXRvciBmb3IgbGF0ZXIgc3RlcHMu "} What happens to a censored patient in the Kaplan-Meier calculation? - They are counted as a death at the time of censoring in the data - They stay at risk until censored, then leave with no drop - They are removed from the whole analysis from the very start of it - They are counted as surviving until the end of the study period ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s2q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="eykweb.muhgrs" data-show="VGhlIHJpZ2h0IGVuZCBvZiB0aGUgY3VydmUgcmVzdHMgb24gZmV3IHBhdGllbnRzIGFuZCBp cyB1bnJlbGlhYmxl" data-explain="VGhlIHRhaWwgb2YgdGhlIGN1cnZlIGlzIGVzdGltYXRlZCBmcm9tIHRoZSBmZXcgcGF0aWVu dHMgc3RpbGwgZm9sbG93ZWQsIHNvIGl0IGlzIHVuc3RhYmxlLiBUaGUgcmlzayB0YWJsZSBz aG93cyBob3cgbXVjaCBkYXRhIHN1cHBvcnQgZWFjaCBwYXJ0IG9mIHRoZSBjdXJ2ZS4="} Why should a Kaplan-Meier plot show the number at risk beneath the curve? - It gives the p-value for the comparison made between the two groups - It shows the hazard ratio for each one of the groups in the plot - The right end of the curve rests on few patients and is unreliable - It is included only to make the plot look more complete and tidy ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s2q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="eyl9n1.muhv96" data-show="QWJvdXQgNzIlIG9mIEhJVi1wb3NpdGl2ZSBwYXRpZW50cyBhcmUgZXN0aW1hdGVkIGFsaXZl IGF0IDEyIG1vbnRocw==" data-explain="UygxMikgaXMgdGhlIHByb2JhYmlsaXR5IG9mIHN1cnZpdmluZyBiZXlvbmQgMTIgbW9udGhz LCBzbyA3MiUgc3Vydml2ZSB0byB0aGF0IHBvaW50IGFuZCAyOCUgaGF2ZSBkaWVkIGJ5IHRo ZW4uIEl0IGlzIG5vdCBhIGhhemFyZCwgYSBtZWRpYW4sIG9yIHRoZSBwcm9wb3J0aW9uIHdo byBkaWVkLg=="} At 12 months the Kaplan-Meier survival for HIV-positive patients is 0.72. How should this be stated? - 72% of HIV-positive patients died within 12 months of starting treatment - The hazard of dying in the HIV-positive group is 0.72 per month of time - The median survival of HIV-positive patients is about 0.72 of a year - About 72% of HIV-positive patients are estimated alive at 12 months ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s2q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="eylmvn.mui9qg" data-show="SXQgY2Fubm90IGJlIGVzdGltYXRlZCBmcm9tIHRoZXNlIGRhdGE=" data-explain="S2FwbGFuLU1laWVyIGNhbm5vdCBleHRyYXBvbGF0ZSBiZXlvbmQgdGhlIGRhdGEuIFJlcG9y dGluZyBzdXJ2aXZhbCBhdCB0aW1lcyB3aXRoIG5vIG9uZSBhdCByaXNrIHdvdWxkIGJlIGlu dmVudGlvbi4="} What is the survival estimate at 30 months if the longest follow-up in the data is 24 months? - It cannot be estimated from these data - It is the same as the survival at 24 months - It is zero, since nobody was followed that long - It equals the median survival of the cohort ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - KM estimates survival with a **step function**; censored patients **leave the risk set** - Report **survival at fixed times** with CI; the **median** may be 'not reached' - Always show the **number at risk**; beware the thin right tail - KM is **descriptive**: the log-rank test and Cox model compare groups ::: **Next:** Session 3: comparing curves

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
